final_text:
I give up.

The file still compiles with only the original `declaration uses sorry` warning, and the Mathlib lemmas I checked (`Matrix.det_pow`, `Matrix.submatrix_mul`, `Matrix.det_submatrix_equiv_self`, `Matrix.det_fromBlocks_one₁₁`) exist. But I do not have a mathematical argument that I can formalize.

The obstacle is the core claim: that `A` very odd implies `A^k` very odd for all `k`. Principal minors of `A^k` do not reduce to principal minors of `A` in any simple way. A proof would need either the official Putnam characterization of very odd matrices mod 2 or a Schur-complement style argument, and I could not reconstruct either reliably. Formalizing that in Lean would be a large project beyond this attempt.

I left `/work/putnam_2021_b5.lean` unchanged. I also created two scratch files, `/work/scratch_check.lean` and `/work/scratch_check2.lean`, which can be deleted.
